seo.title: Kiro vs HagiCode: Features and Comparison
seo.description: Kiro is Kiro's terminal agent; HagiCode is a workbench that runs it. Compare features, credit pricing and fit, and when Kiro alone is enough.

summary: Kiro is the terminal agent in the Kiro family, running on Kiro credits; HagiCode is a workbench that can run it as an executor. This page compares features, pricing and when Kiro alone is enough.

content: Kiro is Kiro's terminal agent: you run `kiro-cli` in a project, and it reads your `.kiro/` steering files and MCP config, then edits code and runs commands using your Kiro plan. HagiCode is a desktop and web workbench that launches `kiro-cli` as one of its Agent CLIs, adding parallel sessions, proposals and commits. It does not replace Kiro and it does not sell Kiro credits.

If you already work in Kiro and want its agents, steering and hooks in a terminal, stay with Kiro alone. Add HagiCode when you run several tasks at once or want a proposal workflow independent of Kiro's own.

sections.title: Kiro vs HagiCode at a glance

cells: What it is
Terminal agent from Kiro; shares core capabilities with other Kiro surfaces
Desktop and web AI programming workbench that drives Agent CLIs you install
Interface and platforms
Terminal chat started with `kiro-cli`; macOS, Linux, Windows 11 (PowerShell)
Desktop app for Windows, macOS, Linux; Docker Compose container; Microsoft Store edition
Pricing and licensing
Part of Kiro plans: Free (50 credits/month), Pro $20, Pro+ $40, Power $200 per month, as of October 2026
Desktop and Container free; Store edition free with optional one-time TurboEngine purchase
Model and provider access
Built on Claude models; an Auto agent picks, and `/model` lets you choose per chat
Hosts no models; uses whatever `kiro-cli` is signed in with, so cost stays in Kiro credits
Parallel work
One chat per terminal; custom agents; cloud sessions keep running after you disconnect
Several concurrent sessions across repos, managed from an Agents view
Spec and planning workflow
Plan agent explores code without modifying it; steering files carry team rules
OpenSpec proposals: propose, validate, apply, archive; 3 concurrent on free editions, 32 with TurboEngine
Git and commit handling
Runs shell and Git commands; headless mode can open pull requests in pipelines
AI-composed commits, Git management, GitHub integration, embedded Code Server editor
Setup effort
`curl -fsSL https://cli.kiro.dev/install | bash`, then browser sign-in
Install HagiCode Desktop, with a working, signed-in `kiro-cli` already on the machine
Best for
Developers on Kiro plans who want agents, steering and hooks in the terminal or CI
Developers running several tasks or repos who want a GUI and a spec discipline

items.title: Custom agents with scoped permissions
content: You can define agents with pre-set prompts and tool permissions, then start one with `kiro-cli --agent <name>`. That is a practical way to give a reviewer agent read-only tools and a builder agent more room, all from files.

items.title: Steering and shared project config
content: The CLI reads steering files and MCP configuration from the project's `.kiro/` folder, the same place other Kiro surfaces use, so team rules carry across the IDE and terminal. Agent skills, a knowledge base and code intelligence build on that.

items.title: Hooks, plan agent and cloud sessions
content: Hooks automate steps before and after commands, a plan agent explores code without editing it, and cloud sessions keep running after you disconnect. Together they suit longer tasks you want to leave running.

items.title: Headless mode and ACP
content: Headless mode runs prompts non-interactively in CI/CD with API keys, for example to troubleshoot a failing build or open a pull request. ACP support lets compatible IDEs drive the CLI. Sign-in works with Google, GitHub, AWS Builder ID or an organisation identity.

sections.title: When to choose Kiro, and when to choose HagiCode

items: You already use Kiro and want its agents, steering files and hooks in the terminal.
You want custom agents with tightly scoped tool permissions defined in files.
You need headless runs in CI/CD with API keys.
You want long tasks to keep running in cloud sessions after you disconnect.
You work on one task at a time and want no extra application.
You run several Kiro tasks across repositories and want the sessions side by side.
You want an OpenSpec proposal, validation and archive step, and the proposal lifecycle is not tied to one vendor.
You prefer to review tool calls and diffs in a GUI, with AI-composed commits and Code Server.
You want Vault notes and Monospecs for shared context across Kiro sessions and repositories.
You mix Agent CLIs (Kiro, Claude Code, Codex and others) and want one workspace.

blocks.title: Where HagiCode is not the right tool
content: Headless CI/CD jobs and scripted one-shot runs: use Kiro's headless mode directly.
You only want a terminal, or a quick question in an editor you already use.
Teams that do not want proposal and spec discipline, or who are happy with Kiro's own steering and spec features; free editions also cap concurrent proposals at 3.
It needs `kiro-cli` installed and signed in first, so it adds setup compared with Kiro alone.
HagiCode accepts only `kiro-cli` binaries; the generic `kiro` launcher is rejected so it never starts the desktop app by accident.
HagiCode starts the `kiro-cli` you already installed, in its ACP mode (`kiro-cli acp`), and shows the session in its own interface. Your install, sign-in and Kiro credits stay as they were.
Nothing is locked in: your repositories stay ordinary Git repositories and you can run `kiro-cli` in a terminal at any time.

items: 1. Install Kiro (`curl -fsSL https://cli.kiro.dev/install | bash`; for Windows see the installation page on kiro.dev) and sign in; `kiro-cli login` re-authenticates.
2. Install HagiCode Desktop (free) for Windows, macOS or Linux.
3. In HagiCode, choose Kiro as the Agent CLI for a session.
4. Open a repository and start a session or an OpenSpec proposal.
5. Expect Kiro models and credit usage as before; HagiCode adds workflow around them.
6. To go back to plain Kiro, open a terminal in the same repository and run `kiro-cli`.

blocks.title: What works for Kiro inside HagiCode
content: Works: parallel sessions, OpenSpec proposals, AI commits, Code Server, Vault, Monospecs and the unified tool-call view with Kiro.
Does not apply to Kiro: interactive questions (Claude, Pi, OMP and Reasonix only) and the agent work panel (Claude only).
Kiro-specific features such as cloud sessions and custom-agent selection live in Kiro itself; HagiCode talks to it over ACP.

sections.title: What HagiCode adds on top of any agent

items.title: Parallel sessions and Agents management
content: Kiro gives you one chat per terminal. HagiCode can keep several Kiro sessions running across repositories and list them in one Agents view.

items.title: OpenSpec proposals
content: Kiro has steering files for standing rules. An OpenSpec proposal covers a single change: written, validated, applied and archived, so you keep the reasoning behind it.

items.title: AI commits and Code Server
content: HagiCode composes the commit message from what Kiro changed, and the embedded Code Server lets you check the edits without leaving the workbench.

items.title: Monospecs and Vault
content: Monospecs lets a Kiro session span several repositories; Vault stores notes that outlast one session.

items.title: One tool-call view and optional TokenMonitor
content: Kiro's tool calls show in the same layout as other agents' calls, and an optional TokenMonitor can show usage in the status bar. Kiro credits and billing are unchanged.

items: Kiro is a capable terminal agent with custom agents, steering, hooks and headless mode; for one terminal and one task it is enough alone.
HagiCode is a workbench layer that runs `kiro-cli` underneath, adding sessions, proposals and commits rather than credits or models.
Use Kiro directly for CI; use HagiCode for parallel, reviewed work.

faq.question: Is Kiro free?
faq.answer: Kiro has a free plan with 50 credits per month, plus Pro ($20), Pro+ ($40) and Power ($200) plans per month, as of October 2026. The CLI has no separate pricing and uses your Kiro plan; see kiro.dev/pricing.

faq.question: How do I install Kiro?
faq.answer: On macOS and Linux run `curl -fsSL https://cli.kiro.dev/install | bash`, then start `kiro-cli` and sign in through the browser. Windows 11 (PowerShell) is supported; see the installation page on kiro.dev for the command.

faq.question: Can I use Kiro with HagiCode?
faq.answer: Yes. Install `kiro-cli` and sign in, then choose Kiro as the Agent CLI in HagiCode. HagiCode accepts only `kiro-cli` binaries, not the generic `kiro` launcher.

faq.question: Does HagiCode replace Kiro?
faq.answer: No. HagiCode runs Kiro as its executor and adds sessions, proposals, commits and a GUI around it.

faq.question: Kiro vs HagiCode: which should I pick?
faq.answer: Use Kiro alone for single-terminal work, custom agents and CI. Add HagiCode for parallel sessions, OpenSpec proposals and a visual workspace.
